## Overview

`cpmr`'s primary workflow is a native, matrix-first API built around
`spec()` together with `cpm()`.

This vignette walks through:

- how to shape CPM inputs;
- how to run leakage-safe fold-based assessment;
- how to inspect predictions and selected edges;
- how custom resamples and missing-data handling work.

## Prepare Inputs

CPM expects one row per subject and one column per edge.

- `conmat`: an `n x p` connectivity matrix;
- `behav`: a length-`n` numeric outcome vector;
- `covariates`: an optional `n x q` nuisance matrix.

```{r}
library(cpmr)

withr::local_seed(123)
n <- 80
p <- 200

conmat <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)
covariates <- matrix(rnorm(n), ncol = 1)
behav <- rowMeans(conmat[, 1:12, drop = FALSE]) +
  0.5 * covariates[, 1] +
  rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)
```

## Run CPM with `cpm()`

Use `cpm()` on a `spec()` object for an out-of-sample estimate of predictive
performance.

```{r}
result <- cpm(
  conmat = conmat,
  behav = behav,
  spec = spec(),
  covariates = covariates,
  resamples = 5
)

result
summary(result)
```

This keeps CPM-specific steps such as covariate handling, edge selection, and
model training inside each assessment fold.

## Inspect Predictions and Edges

CPM results keep observation-level predictions on the object, while
`summary()` reports pooled RMSE and MAE, pooled out-of-fold correlations, and
mean fold-wise correlations. Use `tidy()` to obtain pooled metrics or the
per-fold correlation table.

```{r}
predictions <- result$predictions

summary_result <- summary(result)

summary_result
head(summary_result[["metrics"]])
head(predictions)
head(tidy(result, component = "metrics"))
head(tidy(result, component = "metrics", level = "pooled"))
```

These three outputs have slightly different jobs:

- `summary(result)` prints the default aggregate report;
- `summary(result)[["metrics"]]` exposes the compact summary-level metric
  table stored on the summary object;
- `tidy(result, component = "metrics")` returns the raw fold-wise metric
  table for further filtering, plotting, or export, while
  `level = "pooled"` returns pooled metrics.

By default, `cpm()` uses 10-fold assessment and `return_edges = "sum"`. Ten
folds require at least 10 complete cases; around 30 cases are a rough minimum
for at least 3 observations per assessment fold, not a guarantee of stable
correlations. Smaller assessment folds trigger a warning, prioritize RMSE and
MAE, and mark pooled out-of-fold correlations as descriptive. Explicit
leave-one-out assessment is available with `resamples = NULL`.

## Tune the selection level

When comparing several edge-selection levels, `selection_levels` performs
inner-fold selection separately within each outer training set. The outer
assessment fold is excluded from that choice and is used only to estimate
performance. The default objective is the mean inner-fold RMSE; set
`selection_metric = "mae"` to select by mean MAE instead. Separate-sign
construction selects by the `joint` prediction stream, while net construction
selects by `net`. Inner-fold candidate scores and selected levels are available
through `tidy(..., component = "tuning")`. The nested results estimate the
performance of the selection procedure, and the selected level may differ
across outer folds.

```{r tune-selection-level}
tuned_result <- cpm(
  conmat = conmat,
  behav = behav,
  spec = spec(),
  resamples = 5,
  selection_levels = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05),
  selection_metric = "rmse",
  inner_resamples = 4,
  return_edges = "none"
)

summary(tuned_result)
tidy(tuned_result, component = "tuning")
```

Each inner-fold association vector is computed once and reused across the
candidate levels for that split. No cached statistics are retained between
folds or calls, so changes to folds, covariates, or selection settings cannot
reuse stale values. Use `set.seed()` when reproducible random inner folds are
needed. Nested tuning costs more than a fixed-specification run because each
outer training set evaluates every candidate across its inner folds.

By default, `cpm()` stores fold-aggregated edge
selection counts. This makes edge summaries immediately available in the common
fold-based workflow.

If you want to control edge storage explicitly:

```{r}
edge_result <- cpm(
  conmat = conmat,
  behav = behav,
  spec = spec(),
  covariates = covariates,
  resamples = 5,
  return_edges = "sum"
)

dim(edge_result$edges)
```

`predictions` returns one row per original observation. If
`na_action = "exclude"` removed subjects before fitting, those rows are still
present and their `fold` value is `NA`.

When `return_edges = "sum"`, `cpmr` stores fold-summed edge counts for each
edge. If memory matters, switch to `return_edges = "none"` or use
`return_edges = "all"` only when fold-wise edge arrays are truly needed.

## Custom Resamples

If you already have a partition scheme, pass it through `resamples`.

```{r}
custom_resamples <- split(
  seq_len(n),
  cut(seq_len(n), breaks = 4, labels = FALSE)
)

custom_obj <- cpm(
  conmat = conmat,
  behav = behav,
  spec = spec(),
  resamples = custom_resamples,
  return_edges = "none"
)

summary(custom_obj)
```

Custom resamples must:

- be supplied as assessment-row indices;
- cover every complete-case subject exactly once;
- not overlap across folds.

When `na_action = "exclude"`, those indices still refer to original row numbers
of the complete-case subjects kept in the analysis.

## Missing-Data Handling

Set `na_action = "exclude"` if you want `cpmr` to fit on complete cases while
preserving original row positions in the outputs.

```{r}
behav_with_na <- behav
behav_with_na[c(3, 11)] <- NA_real_

na_obj <- cpm(
  conmat = conmat,
  behav = behav_with_na,
  spec = spec(),
  resamples = 5,
  na_action = "exclude"
)

na_predictions <- na_obj$predictions
na_predictions[na_predictions$row %in% c(3, 11), ]
```

This behavior matters when you need to merge predictions back to subject-level
metadata after assessment.

- keep a `spec()` object around when you want an explicit reusable
